description: Slowloris-style attack against an externally-launched HTTP/1.1 target. N concurrent TCP connections open, each writing a partial request header byte-by-byte with a sleep between bytes; never sends the final CRLF CRLF that completes the headers. PRIMARY CHECK: after attack_duration_seconds + cooldown_seconds, target serves clean GET /health with 200 OK within max_response_ms. SECONDARY CHECK: process RSS delta within rss_growth_pct_max (no leaked connection state).
loopback_caveat: Loopback can mask socket-buffer effects relative to network paths. transport_mode=loopback-h1 mandatory.

attack_profile.note: Bumping connection_count >= the target's max-connections limit is the point of the test. The harness does NOT enforce a cap; pick connection_count according to the target's configured limit.

comparison_axis_note: Cross-stack slowloris results are NOT comparable without explicit normalization of (a) max-concurrent-connections, (b) header-receive-timeout, (c) idle-connection-eviction interval. Different runtimes have different defaults; comparison without normalizing these is apples-to-oranges. Label connection_count, header_delay_seconds, attack_duration_seconds in any cross-stack report row.
